prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1444; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision you were involved in. Do you understand that this conversation is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving on the main road in Baytown, heading toward the shopping center. It was a clear afternoon, and traffic was moderate.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I was going about thirty miles an hour. A car came over into my lane from the opposite direction. I tried to swerve, but there wasn't enough room, and we made contact nose to nose.

Q: How fast do you think the other vehicle was traveling?

A: I honestly couldn't say. It didn't seem like it was going very fast, maybe twenty or twenty-five.

Q: Did either airbag deploy?

A: No, they didn't. It was more of a jolt than a hard crash.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?

A: I did, but I felt stiff right away. My neck was sore and my lower back started aching within an hour or so.

Q: Have you sought medical attention since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that evening. They diagnosed me with a neck strain and a lower back strain and told me to rest and take anti-inflammatories.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. My neck is still tender when I turn my head, and I get a dull ache in my lower back after sitting for long periods. I'm following up with my doctor next week.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think I've covered it. I'm just hoping to get my recovery on track.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.

A: Thank you.
